decisions.reason: As a dental consumable line closely tied to the firm's core laboratory business, a product that has remained in the portfolio this long would usually be kept unless demand had clearly disappointed.
The PETG thermoforming blank fits the established dental materials range and specialist trade channels, so a large German manufacturer would normally retain it as a standard portfolio item.

The UV-curing lacquer still appears somewhat more vulnerable because it had weaker strategic visibility, but it complements laboratory workflows and is not likely enough to be withdrawn now to justify dropping it.
The intraoral contrast spray supports digital dental workflows that match the firm's innovation path, making continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.

Custom hearing protection earmolds are more niche than the main dental lines, but they use the same custom-manufacturing capabilities and hearing-care channels, so management would usually keep them on the market.
